newsitem.title: UK: Ferguson Intl warns on H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Ferguson Intl warns on H1 profits.

text.p: British label manufacturer Ferguson International Holdings Plc said on Wednesday its first-half pretax profit would be lower than expected but not less than 5.0 million stg.
The profit forecast for the six months to August 31 included a property profit of about 500,000 stg.
Ferguson also predicted its profit for the year would be close to last year's 10.6 million stg pretax profit from continuing operations.
The company said its chief executive, David J. Watson, had resigned immediately, less than a year after having been named to the board in October.
Ferguson's shares sank nearly 12 percent, dropping 19p to 145 to rank among the London market's top percentage losers at 1045 GMT.
Ferguson blamed the profit shortfall on disruptions caused by relocations at two of its plants, including the one at Pan Yu in China.
"It is believed that the problems will have been resolved by the end of the first half, but it is unlikely that the lost profit will be recovered in the second half," the company said in a statement.
However, it said it expected to maintain its interim and final dividiends.
